answer: Pigment-marked stake bonds: each new identity must lock a refundable deposit tinted by a unique on-chain pigment — a hash of its verified work history — before it can transact. The bond is slashed if two identities share the same cedar-rooted device attestation, so one machine cannot spawn many accounts. A thread of sequential, time-locked tasks must then be completed before voting rights unlock, making each fake identity pay the full bond plus real labor, while honest agents earn the bond back with interest.
